  %\VignetteIndexEntry{CTTIR v5 and project logos}

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(hexmakR)
```

The v5 library contains 45 identities. Named designs place the exact package
name inside the lower part of the hex, with the native R scientific artwork
above. The exterior is transparent. Light, dark and monochrome modes share
this layout. The original 1,035 assets are included unchanged.

```{r catalogue}
head(hex_catalog())
```

Create an editable design or locate an approved original:

```{r design, eval=FALSE}
design <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
print(design)
hex_export(design, "phenoscapR.svg")
hex_export(design, "phenoscapR.png", width = 1600)
hex_asset("phenoscapR", mode = "dark", layout = "lockup", format = "pdf")
```

Project logos can use hexagonal, regular pentagonal or square frames. Choose
any CTTIR motif and palette as a starting point, or a generic built-in icon:

```{r projects, eval=FALSE}
project <- logo_design("My project", motif = "phenoscapR", shape = "pentagon")
hex_export(project, "project.svg")
study <- logo_design("Study", shape = "square", icon = "microscope")
hex_export(study, "study.pdf")
```

Shapes use the same design object, palette roles, editable layers and project
format. Pentagonal and square exports have square canvases. Hexagonal masters
use the width/height ratio sqrt(3)/2. The `layout = "motif"` option exports the
standalone artwork on a transparent square without a frame or name.

Inspect and modify vector geometry:

```{r layers}
design <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
head(hex_layers(design))
```

```{r edit, eval=FALSE}
# Layer 1 is the frame. Shape IDs are deterministic within a composition.
edited <- hex_edit_layer(design, "layer_0001", fill = "#193E36")
# Move or recolour an individual shape; the input object stays unchanged.
edited <- hex_edit_layer(edited, "layer_0005", dx = 0.03, fill = "#45B59A")
hex_save_design(edited, "project.json")
restored <- hex_read_design("project.json")
hex_recipe(restored, "reproduce.R")
```

Coordinates refer to each shape's local viewport. Fill, stroke, line width,
opacity, visibility, translation, scale and explicit point coordinates can be
edited. Artwork is clipped to its frame. Changes to a silhouette can alter
its scientific meaning; review the result at full size and icon size.
Changing the composition, frame or icon in the editor resets shape overrides;
Undo can restore the previous design. The original assets are never modified.

```{r editor, eval=FALSE}
hexmakr_app(package = "phenoscapR")
hexmakr_app(workspace = "classic")
```

Select a package, shape and name, then **Apply design**. Choose a vector layer,
optionally highlight it, edit its properties, then **Apply shape edit**. The
point editor can load the original coordinates for manual adjustment.
**Save project** downloads JSON; **Open saved project** resumes that work.
PNG, SVG, PDF and R-recipe downloads use the current saved design settings.
Pending form changes take effect only after Apply. JSON loading validates
fields and never evaluates uploaded R code.

The bundled JetBrains Mono font supplies outlined name glyphs, so vector
exports do not depend on installed fonts. The shipped font OFL licences are
in `system.file("cttir/source/fonts", package = "hexmakR")`.

```{r regenerate, eval=FALSE}
# 45 x (2 layouts x 3 modes x 3 formats + 5 icons) = 1,035 exports
hex_render_catalog("exports")
```

The twelve catalogue names present only in the older hexstickers repository
are preserved as legacy SVG references under `cttir/legacy`. They are not
claimed as approved v5 motifs. `hexmakeR` maps to `hexmakR`; `delphyR` maps to
`delphyr`. Archive and asset hashes document the imported source material.

The identities `CTTIR` and `cttiR` differ only in case. To prevent collisions
on macOS and Windows, the organisation's asset folder is `CTTIR-brand`; the
R package retains `cttiR`. `hex_catalog()$asset_dir` records the mapping, and
asset lookup, the gallery and batch rendering use it. Displayed names remain
exact. Original assets were re-imported directly from distinct ZIP entries.
